content:
Hiking backpacks in Nairobi are easiest to choose if you start with size: a 20-30 litre daypack for day hikes such as Ngong Hills or Mt Longonot, 35-50 litres for an overnight camp, and 55-70 litres for a multi-day trek like Mt Kenya. Then get the fit right, and check the build quality before you pay.

Most hikers buy the wrong pack because it looked good on a hook, not because it fitted their back or their trips. This guide to hiking backpacks in Nairobi explains which pack size you need, how to fit one to your torso, what to look for in new and thrifted packs, how to care for a pack, and where to buy one on Thika Road.

Quick Facts

  • Day hikes: a 20-30 litre daypack carries water, snacks, a rain jacket and a warm layer
  • Overnight camping: 35-50 litres fits a sleeping bag, mat and cooking kit
  • Multi-day treks: 55-70 litres suits Mt Kenya or Kilimanjaro if you carry your own kit
  • Fit: pack size follows torso length (base of the neck to the top of the hip bones), not height
  • Weather: a rain cover or dry bag liner matters in the long rains (March-May) and short rains (October-December)
  • Where to buy: try hiking backpacks in Nairobi at Mountain Mall, 3rd Floor, Shop D39, Thika Road, or order online

What Size Hiking Backpack Do You Need?

The right backpack size depends on how long you will be out and what you must carry. A day hike needs 20-30 litres, an overnight trip 35-50 litres, and a multi-day trek with your own tent and food 55-70 litres.

Volume is measured in litres and covers the main compartment plus pockets. Bigger is not better: a half-empty 60 litre pack sags, swings and pulls you backwards on steep ground, while an overstuffed 20 litre pack forces you to strap a jacket to the outside where it snags on thorny bush. When comparing hiking backpacks in Nairobi, pick the size for the trips you do most often, not the one big trek you might do next year.

Is a 25 litre daypack enough for a day hike near Nairobi?

A 25 litre daypack is enough for almost every day hike near Nairobi. It holds two to three litres of water, lunch, a rain jacket, a fleece and a small first aid kit, with room left for a headlamp in case you finish after dark.

Among hiking backpacks in Nairobi, a daypack with a hydration sleeve is worth considering for hot, exposed hikes such as the Mt Longonot crater rim, where shade is scarce and you need to sip often. Our Mt Longonot hike guide explains why water is the heaviest thing in most day packs.

What size backpack do you need for Mt Kenya?

For Mt Kenya you need a 55-70 litre pack if you carry your own tent, sleeping bag and food, or a 25-35 litre daypack if porters carry your main bag. Most organised Mt Kenya climbs use porters, so check with your operator first.

If you are using porters, the porter usually carries a duffel bag, while you carry a daypack with water, snacks, a warm jacket, gloves and rain gear. Our guide on what to pack for hiking Mt Kenya lists everything that goes into both bags.

How Do You Choose Hiking Backpacks in Nairobi That Fit?

Choose hiking backpacks in Nairobi by torso length and hip size, not by your height or the pack's colour. A pack that fits puts most of the load on your hips, so your shoulders and lower back stay comfortable for hours.

Two people of the same height can need different pack sizes because torso length varies a lot. Many larger hiking backpacks in Nairobi shops come in sizes (S, M, L) or have an adjustable back system, while most small daypacks come in one size that suits a wide range of people. Women's-specific packs usually have a shorter back, narrower shoulder straps and a more curved hip belt.

How do you measure your torso length for a backpack?

Measure your torso from the bony bump at the base of your neck (the C7 vertebra) down to the line between the tops of your hip bones. Ask a friend to do it with a soft tape measure while you stand straight.

  1. Tilt your head forward and find the most prominent bone at the base of your neck.
  2. Put your hands on your hips with your thumbs pointing backwards along the top of your hip bones.
  3. Have a friend measure along your spine from the neck bone to the imaginary line between your thumbs.
  4. Compare the result with the size chart on the pack's label or the maker's website; most hiking backpacks in Nairobi shops show a torso range.
  5. Load the pack with 5-8 kg, put it on, and fasten the hip belt first so it sits over your hip bones.
  6. Tighten the shoulder straps, then the load lifters, and walk around for at least ten minutes.

Why does the hip belt matter on a hiking backpack?

The hip belt matters because your legs and hips carry weight far better than your shoulders. On any pack above about 30 litres, a padded hip belt that wraps your hip bones is essential.

On small daypacks a thin webbing belt is fine, as it only stops the pack swinging. When you try overnight and trekking hiking backpacks in Nairobi, the belt padding should cover the top of your hip bones with the buckle roughly over your belly button. If the belt sits on your waist or slides down to your thighs, the torso size is wrong.

What Should You Look for When Buying Hiking Backpacks in Nairobi?

When buying hiking backpacks in Nairobi, look at fit first, then the back panel, hip belt, zips, buckles, fabric and pockets. Five minutes of hands-on checking tells you more than any brand name.

Are thrifted hiking backpacks in Nairobi worth buying?

Thrifted hiking backpacks in Nairobi are worth buying when the frame, hip belt, zips and buckles are sound. A well-made pack from a good brand often lasts many years, so a pre-owned one can give you better build quality for your budget than a cheap new pack.

Before buying thrifted hiking backpacks in Nairobi, open and close every zip, clip every buckle, pull hard on the shoulder strap seams and look inside for flaking waterproof coating. Smell matters too: a musty smell can mean the pack was stored damp. Our shop sells quality thrifted gear alongside some new items, which makes a good pack affordable.

Do you need a rain cover for your backpack?

Yes, you need some rain protection for your backpack on most Kenyan hikes, because few pack fabrics are fully waterproof at the seams and zips. A fitted rain cover or a dry bag liner inside the pack keeps your spare layers and phone dry.

A heavy-duty bin bag inside the pack works as a cheap liner, which helps because many hiking backpacks in Nairobi, new or thrifted, come without a cover. If you hike often in the rainy seasons, read our guide to rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi to keep yourself as dry as your kit.

Pro Tips: Packing Your Backpack

  • Heavy in the middle: pack water and food close to your back, between your shoulder blades
  • Light at the bottom: a sleeping bag or soft layers fill the base of an overnight pack
  • Rain gear on top: keep your rain jacket where you can reach it in seconds
  • Small items in pockets: sunscreen, snacks and a phone go in hip belt or lid pockets
  • Day pack weight: aim to keep a day pack under about 10% of your body weight
  • Adjust on the move: loosen the hip belt slightly on descents and tighten it on climbs

How Should You Care for a Hiking Backpack?

Care for a hiking backpack by emptying it after every hike, brushing out dust and grass seeds, and drying it fully in the shade. Wash it by hand with mild soap when it gets dirty, never in a washing machine.

Strong sun breaks down nylon and the polyurethane coating inside many packs, so dry yours on a shaded line rather than on a hot roof. Wipe the zips clean after dusty hikes such as Hell's Gate, because grit wears the sliders. Store the pack loosely, unzipped and somewhere dry, not squashed under a bed in a damp corner. The pack maker Deuter's backpack cleaning guide gives step-by-step washing advice.

Small repairs keep a pack going for years. A loose stitch on a shoulder strap or a split seam can be fixed by a local tailor for a small cost, and spare buckles are easy to fit. Replace a damaged pack before a big trek, not halfway up the mountain.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much should I spend on hiking backpacks in Nairobi?

Hiking backpacks in Nairobi are worth spending more on than most other items, because a poor fit ruins every hike. Quality thrifted packs give you a well-made brand-name pack for a lower price than new. Compare current prices on our product pages and choose the best-fitting pack your budget allows, rather than the biggest or cheapest one.

Can I use a school or laptop backpack for hiking?

A school or laptop backpack works for a short, flat walk such as Karura Forest, but it is a poor choice for longer hikes. Laptop bags lack a hip belt, ventilated back panel and side bottle pockets, so the weight hangs on your shoulders and your back gets soaked in sweat. A proper 20-30 litre hiking daypack is far more comfortable.

What is the difference between a daypack and a trekking backpack?

A daypack is a small pack of about 15-30 litres for a single day, usually with a light frame sheet and a thin hip belt. A trekking backpack holds 50 litres or more, with a stiff frame, padded hip belt and load lifters to carry a tent, sleeping bag and food for several days in comfort.

Is a hydration pack better than water bottles?

A hydration pack is better for hot, steady hikes because you can sip through a tube without stopping, which helps you drink enough. Water bottles are easier to refill, clean and track. Many Kenyan hikers carry a 2-3 litre bladder in their pack plus one bottle in a side pocket for mixing electrolytes.

Do hiking backpacks come in women's sizes?

Many hiking backpacks in Nairobi come in women's versions with a shorter torso, narrower and curved shoulder straps and a more angled hip belt. A women's pack is not required, though. The best choice is whichever pack matches your torso length and feels comfortable when loaded, so try both styles before you decide.

Final Thoughts

Choosing hiking backpacks in Nairobi comes down to three steps: pick the right size for your usual trips, fit it to your torso and hips, and check the zips, buckles, seams and fabric before you buy. A well-fitted 25-30 litre daypack covers most hikes around Nairobi, while Mt Kenya and longer treks need more.
